newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeri court convicts five on spying for Iran.
newsitem.headline: Azeri court convicts five on spying for Iran.

text.p: A Baku court on Monday convicted five Azeris, including four leaders of the Islamic Party, of spying for Iran.

"Their main goal was to strengthen anti-Western propaganda and carry out protests against the participation of American and Western oil companies in projects in Azerbaijan," prosecutor Bahram Zahidov said.
The convicted included the head of Azerbaijan's Islamic Party Alikram Aliyev, who was sentenced to 11 years, as well as three other party officials, who received ten-year sentences.
A fifth man, the director of a tourist firm who prepared false passports, was sentenced to two years in prison.
After the verdict was ready, Aliyev shouted out in court: "We were not engaged in espionage. The court and the judges are participating in provocations set up by the KGB."
His lawyer said Aliyev had received $50,000 from Iran, but for charitable purposes only such as helping children.
A high-placed Azeri government official said afterwards that the verdict would likely hurt relations with Tehran.
"The unveiling of these facts will have a negative impact on Iranian-Azerbaijan relations," said the official.

The speaker of Iran's parliament, Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, on a visit to Moscow on Saturday, said Azerbaijan was making a big mistake by disagreeing with Iran and other nations in the region on the status of the Caspian Sea and its offshore oil deposits.
